chunks: And what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man on a journey who does not find water, so he performs tayammum, then prays, then comes upon water while some of the time still remains: should he proceed on the basis of his prayer, or should he perform wudu and repeat the salat (prayer)? He said: He should proceed on the basis of his prayer, for indeed the Lord of water is the Lord of earth.

key_terms.التُّرَابِ: earth; the material used for tayammum
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the state in which the questioner describes the man
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer); the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water; the normal means of purification for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: the prayer time; part of it still remained after he found water
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: he performed tayammum; dry ablution used when water is unavailable
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: he performs wudu (ablution); ritual washing with water

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and later finds water before the prayer time ends, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning tayammum during travel. If a person prays with tayammum due to the absence of water and then finds water while time remains, he does not repeat the salat (prayer), because tayammum was a valid divinely sanctioned purification.
